about-us.text: Our General Surgery Research Team, situated at St Boniface General Hospital in Winnipeg Manitoba, is at the forefront of exploring new avenues in clinical trials and surgical simulation. We strive to make meaningful contributions to the field of surgery with our focus on patient care and surgical proficiency.

Clinical Trials: Our team actively engages in clinical trials to assess and implement the latest advancements in surgical procedures, technologies, and treatment modalities, aiming to introduce evidence-based practices that elevate the standard of surgical care and ensure optimal patient outcomes. Our research spans diverse themes, including perioperative optimization of bariatric outcomes, predictors of bariatric surgery outcomes, Indigenous bariatric surgery, and acute care surgery outcomes. We explore areas such as fitness and nutritional outcomes, geography/access to care, family physician experience, sleep apnea, and virtual care in the context of bariatric surgery. Our commitment extends to predicting factors like length of stay, bariatric biomarker profiles, and considering the influence of geography and Indigenous status. Additionally, we conduct foundational work to understand the Indigenous experience with bariatric surgery, aiming to incorporate Indigenous approaches to wellness in bariatric care. Our research themes align with interests in bariatric surgery, minimally invasive surgery, and acute care surgery, all contributing to advancements in surgical knowledge and patient care.

Surgical Simulation: Our team places a strong emphasis on Surgical Simulation, acknowledging the vital role of hands-on training in surgical proficiency. Devoted to the development and refinement of surgical simulation programs, we offer a risk-free environment for surgeons to augment their skills, explore new techniques, and enhance patient safety. In our commitment to innovation, our Surgical Simulation programs integrate cutting-edge technologies such as eye tracking, facial expressions tracking, 3D printing, and more. These advanced tools contribute to the realism and effectiveness of our simulations, offering a comprehensive training experience that aligns with the latest technological advancements in the field of surgery.

team.text: Dr. Hardy completed her Doctor of Medicine (2002) at the University of Toronto and her General Surgery Residency (2008) at the University of Manitoba followed by a Fellowship in Minimally Invasive Surgery at the University of Toronto (2010). Her research training included a Master of Science in Surgery degree at the University of Manitoba during surgical residency. She is a Fellow of the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada as well as the American College of Surgeons.

Dr. Hardy is an Associate Professor at the University of Manitoba with a clinical practice of Minimally Invasive Surgery at St. Boniface General Hospital and Victoria General Hospital. She currently serves as Graduate Chair for the Department of Surgery and is an active member of the Clinician Investigator Program Committee, Research Advisory Committee, Surgery Education Advisory Committee and General Surgery Competency Committee. Dr. Hardy is also the research lead at the Centre for Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery. She actively supervises undergraduate students, medical students, surgical residents, surgical fellows and master’s students in their research activities.

Dr. Vergis completed his Doctor of Medicine (2002) and residency in general surgery (2008) at the University of Manitoba while concurrently earning a Masters of Medical Education through the University of Dundee, Scotland. He then attained a clinical fellowship in Bariatric and Minimally Invasive Surgery at the University of Toronto after obtaining his Canadian and American Board Certifications in surgery.

He is currently a Professor of surgery at the University of Manitoba and is an active member of the minimally invasive surgery program at St. Boniface and Victoria General Hospital. Dr. Vergis holds several clinical leadership positions including clinical lead for the provincial Bariatric Surgery Program and the director of Surgical Peritoneal Dialysis for the Manitoba Renal Program. His educational leadership positions include post graduate surgical skills director, general surgery residency endoscopy director, and the program director for the minimally invasive and bariatric surgery fellowship at the University of Manitoba.

Dr. He brings a rich background in medicine, merging extensive surgical expertise with a profound commitment to advancing healthcare education. Her journey commenced with rigorous medical training at Xinxiang Medical University and Shantou Medical University, where she honed her skills as a surgeon. The pursuit of excellence led her to Canada in 2014, marking a pivotal moment in her career.

A testament to her dedication, Dr. He completed her Ph.D. training at the University of Alberta in 2019, solidifying her position as a thought leader in the field. Currently serving as a Research Associate in the Department of Surgery at the University of Manitoba, she actively engages with a collaborative network that spans surgeons, engineers, clinical educators, and psychologists.

Dr. He’s research is at the forefront of innovation, focusing on the development of simulators and the evaluation of educational outcomes within simulation-based programs. Her long-term vision is leveraging simulation in surgery to enhance care quality and elevate patient safety standards.
